# s393 — Retract a note that turned out wrong

`slicer note-retract ID --note-id NOTE --reason TEXT [--owner ACTOR]` (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) marks one item note as retracted without deleting it. The record keeps its text and gains `retracted_by`, `retracted_at` and `retracted_reason`. The render shows it as retracted. `next --ready` note packing omits it with reason `retracted`, and it no longer satisfies `handoff_requires_note_kind`. History gets a `note-retract` line. An unknown note is refused with `usage` and nothing is written.

**Findings:** ork S65 relay, 2026-10-25 · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-30** — Ready for review: note-retract marks an item note wrong (who/when/why kept; schema 11); retracted notes are dropped from packs, never satisfy handoff_requires_note_kind, render [retracted] and dim in the TUI. Full suite 2961 OK; gate PASS.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** deleting or editing note text (the TUI's existing edit and delete stay as they are), un-retracting, retracting legacy slice notes (`slice-legacy-N` has no record), counting or reporting review failures, and any change to ork, which writes `Review FAIL:` notes (`../ork` `internal/engine/states.go:573`) and keeps that logic.

## Why

A relay orchestrator recorded `Review FAIL: none (reviewer: no blockers)` on ork's S65 because a fix round ran for UI suggestions. That was not a failure. A note cannot be withdrawn, so the slice history shows a false FAIL. `slicer note` (`cmd_note`, `src/slicer/cli.py`) has kinds and `--stale-after` but no retraction. Notes are an audit trail: `mergeindex` treats `note_records` as append-only records keyed by id. A retraction therefore adds fields to the record and never removes it.

Nothing in slicer counts `Review FAIL` notes. The string appears only in the relay contract text in `src/slicer/ai.py`. So retraction needs no counter changes in slicer, but a consumer reading `note_records` sees the new fields.

## Files

- `src/slicer/model.py`: `NoteRecord` gains `retracted_by`, `retracted_at` and `retracted_reason` (strings, default `""`), placed after `stale_after` in `persisted_dict`, `to_dict` (before the derived `trust`) and `from_dict` (type-checked like the other metadata), plus a `retracted` property. `display()` puts a `[retracted]` label where the kind label goes, before it. `rendered()` adds the three fields to its metadata line. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 10 to 11 so an older slicer refuses an index that may hold a retraction, as the note-metadata change did (CHANGELOG, schema 7). Without the bump, an older slicer would drop the fields on its next save.

It looks the record up the same way, refuses an unknown id with `verify_note`'s message and code (`usage`, "has no item note ...; use show --json to find its ID"), refuses a blank or multi-line reason (`usage`) and an already-retracted note (`usage`, naming when and by whom), sets the three fields with `_note_actor(actor(state, owner))` and `_now()`, saves the index and calls `_record(state, item_id, "note-retract", note=record.id, by=...)`. The reason is not put in the log `note` field; the record holds it.

- `test_MergeIndex_RetractedOnOneSide_TakesTheRetraction` (`tests/test_merge_index.py`): base and theirs hold the note unretracted, ours retracted it; the merge keeps one note, retracted.
